title: unify-sdks-auth-retries-streaming-parity-v1.132.0
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Unify authentication, retry semantics, and streaming behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to reduce customer confusion and eliminate parity bugs between runtimes. This PR: 1) standardizes token refresh and fallback auth paths (API key, OAuth token refresh, metadata servers), 2) introduces a shared RetryPolicy semantics (idempotency detection, exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts/timeout) across SDKs, 3) brings TypeScript/Go streaming clients to parity with Python's incremental chunking and function-calling streaming hooks, 4) improves ergonomics for client creation and context-managed lifecycle, and 5) bumps SDK package versions to v1.132.0 with changelogs and migration notes. Implementation notes: - Added unified auth adapter interfaces in each SDK and a small shim to map platform credentials to the shared RetryPolicy. - Merged streaming wire protocol changes: standardized SSE and chunked JSON parsing, unified backpressure signals, and consistent cancel semantics for streaming iterators/async iterators. - Adjusted default retry config: 3 retries for non-streaming idempotent requests; streaming RPCs use a separate retry guard to avoid re-delivering tokens. - Deprecation: legacy `Client.from_api_key` helpers now emit a deprecation warning and call the new `Client.with_auth` factory. Testing: unit and integration tests added for token refresh edge cases, retry backoff jitter bounds, and streaming cancellation. Migration: document includes a short migration guide (see CHANGES.md). Checklist: - [x] Implement auth adapter across Python/TS/Go - [x] Implement shared RetryPolicy and defaults - [x] Streaming parity tests and fixups - [x] Update CI matrix and add integration jobs - [x] Changelogs and release notes - [x] Version bumps to v1.132.0 Rollout plan: will cut SDK releases in coordinated fashion once published packages pass e2e smoke tests. If any regression is reported within 48h we will roll back to previous minor patch while investigating.
